result.document_summary: Massachusetts G.L. c. 186 § 18, the anti-reprisal statute that penalizes landlords for retaliating against tenants who report code violations, enforce housing laws, or join tenants' unions.
result.notes: Section 18 is a tenant anti-retaliation statute. It does not state allowed eviction causes, notice periods, relocation assistance, or a just-cause regime, and it does not cap rent increases, regulate deposits, screening fees, screening restrictions, or algorithmic pricing. It only creates a rebuttable presumption of reprisal for terminations (other than for nonpayment), rent increases, or substantial lease changes within six months of protected activity. This falls outside the six in-scope categories and does not establish a just-cause eviction regime, so no records are extracted.
